lessons.title: A fact and an unmet expectation
lessons.description: Hear a complaint, identify its grounds and keep a condition separate from a promise.
lessons.canDo: Distinguish a visible fact from an expectation

lessons.title: Recognise blame; repair the conversation
lessons.description: Identify an accusing expression and use a calm explanation or apology between peers.
lessons.canDo: Recognise reproach without assuming private intention

grammar.title: An outcome that stays the same
grammar.formation: Verb て/で + も; い-adjective くても (いい→よくても); noun/な-adjective でも. Negative なくても, or nominal でなくても/じゃなくても.
grammar.explanation: Go beyond N4 permission and non-obligation. ても can express even-if or even-though: the outcome holds despite the condition. Facts and context determine whether the condition has happened. Here the group retains viewer choice even if preparation takes time; that promise is distinct from proving preparation complete.
grammar.example: 準備に時間がかかっても、字幕は選べるようにします。
grammar.translation: Even if preparation takes time, we will make the subtitles selectable.

examples.ja: {準備|じゅんび}に{時間|じかん}がかかっても、{字幕|じまく}は{選|えら}べるようにします。
examples.en: Even if preparation takes time, we will make the subtitles selectable.

examples.ja: {不公平|ふこうへい}でも、{相手|あいて}を{傷|きず}つける{言葉|ことば}は{使|つか}いたくありません。
examples.en: Even if it is unfair, I do not want to use words that hurt the other person.

examples.ja: {忙|いそが}しくなくても、{分担|ぶんたん}は{確認|かくにん}します。
examples.en: Even if we are not busy, we will check responsibilities.

grammar.mistake: Noun/な-adjective + でも, not だても. Negative verbs use なくても. A hypothetical inconvenience is not evidence that the inconvenience actually occurred.

grammar.title: A fact contrary to expectation
grammar.formation: Plain verb/い-adjective clause + のに. Present affirmative noun/な-adjective + なのに; past nominal だったのに; nominal negative ではないのに.
grammar.explanation: Retrieve N4 unit 10. のに links an expectation to a contrary fact; it may convey surprise or disappointment. Misaki says she expected selectable subtitles but saw a screen with none. The later explanation identifies a temporary test; the complaint alone does not prove someone broke the policy. Purpose のに is a different construction.
grammar.example: 字幕を選べると聞いたのに、今の画面にはありません。
grammar.translation: Although I heard we could choose subtitles, there are none on the current screen.

examples.ja: {字幕|じまく}を{選|えら}べると{聞|き}いたのに、{今|いま}の{画面|がめん}にはありません。
examples.en: Although I heard we could choose subtitles, there are none on the current screen.

examples.ja: {同|おな}じ{条件|じょうけん}なのに、{二人|ふたり}の{評価|ひょうか}が{違|ちが}います。
examples.en: Although the conditions are the same, the two people’s assessments differ.

examples.ja: {丁寧|ていねい}に{説明|せつめい}したのに、{意図|いと}が{伝|つた}わりませんでした。
examples.en: Although I explained carefully, my intention was not conveyed.

grammar.mistake: 条件なのに uses な, while noun + のくせに uses の in a different pattern. Do not turn the contrast into an unsupported claim about someone’s secret motive or use the purpose のに rule here.

grammar.title: Recognise blame; choose how to repair it
grammar.formation: Attributive plain verb/い-adjective + くせに; noun + のくせに; な-adjective + なくせに. Past verb clauses attach directly.
grammar.explanation: くせに presents a contradiction with reproach. It can sound insulting, even between friends. Recognise it in an accusation, then practice an explanation or neutral statement of what happened. The lesson does not certify the accusation as true. It is not a polite default addressed to a manager.
grammar.example: 「選べると言ったくせに」と、友達を責めました。
grammar.translation: I reproached my friend: “You said we could choose, and yet…”

examples.ja: 「{選|えら}べると{言|い}ったくせに」と、{友達|ともだち}を{責|せ}めました。
examples.en: I reproached my friend: “You said we could choose, and yet…”

examples.ja: 「{担当者|たんとうしゃ}のくせに」と{言|い}うと、{非難|ひなん}が{強|つよ}く{聞|き}こえます。
examples.en: Saying “despite being the person in charge” sounds strongly accusatory.

examples.ja: 「{冷静|れいせい}なくせに」という{言|い}い{方|かた}は、ここでは{使|つか}いません。
examples.en: We will not use the accusing expression “though you act calm” here.

grammar.mistake: Noun の versus な-adjective な is an attachment contrast. Do not use identity stereotypes as evidence of blame. For an ordinary factual disagreement, state the facts and request clarification.

grammar.title: Coexisting states, not two ordinary actions
grammar.formation: Verb ます-stem + ながらも; progressive ていながらも; い-adjective, な-adjective stem or noun + ながらも. Recognise established concessive state/awareness uses.
grammar.explanation: Contrast two qualities or states that coexist. 小さいながらも explains a limited-size café that still supports the activity; 不器用ながらも describes effort despite awkwardness. Ordinary 音楽を聞きながらメモする simply joins actions by one doer; it need not express a concession. Do not infer contrast from も alone.
grammar.example: 店は小さいながらも、二つの画面を比べられます。
grammar.translation: Although the café is small, we can compare two screens.

examples.ja: {店|みせ}は{小|ちい}さいながらも、{二|ふた}つの{画面|がめん}を{比|くら}べられます。
examples.en: Although the café is small, we can compare two screens.

examples.ja: {不器用|ぶきよう}ながらも、{気持|きも}ちを{丁寧|ていねい}に{伝|つた}えました。
examples.en: Despite being awkward, I conveyed my feelings carefully.

examples.ja: {緊張|きんちょう}していながらも、{冷静|れいせい}に{話|はな}しました。
examples.en: Although I was nervous, I spoke calmly.

grammar.mistake: Use the adjective or noun stem: 不器用ながらも, not 不器用なながらも. The set expression 残念ながら is not automatically a productive contrast with も. Read the two coexisting states.

dialogues.title: A screen and an incomplete explanation
dialogues.scene: On Saturday before the three-o’clock film gathering, Misaki sees a subtitle-free screen and believes viewer choice has been lost. Kenta says it is a temporary test. The group has not started the film.

dialogues.title: A pointed remark and a repair
dialogues.scene: After a pointed exchange between these two scenes, Misaki quotes and apologises for her accusatory remark. Kenta explains his response, Bao distinguishes a stated fact from guessed intention, and the friends check selectable subtitles before the film begins.

lines.meaning: A moment ago I reproached you: “You said we could choose, and yet…” Sorry.

lines.romaji: Sono iikata e no hannō de, ore mo tsuyoku itte shimatta. Setsumei o shōryaku shita no wa ore da.
lines.meaning: In reaction to that wording, I spoke sharply too. I was the one who left out the explanation.

glosses.meaning: you said so and yet; accusing quotation

options: She expected selectable subtitles but sees none on the current screen
She cannot find the blue sign
She has been told the gathering is next year
exercises.explain: Misaki explicitly contrasts what she heard with the subtitle-free screen; she already found the landmark.

exercises.prompt: What does Kenta say he is doing?
options: Temporarily testing two screens under the same conditions
Permanently cancelling viewer choice
Moving the café to the university
exercises.explain: Kenta says 今だけ and 同じ条件; this is his explanation, not a secret-intention claim.

exercises.prompt: What does Bao say will remain true even if preparation takes time?
options: Viewers will be able to choose subtitles
All preparation has already finished
Registration no longer has a deadline
exercises.explain: Bao retains the policy with 時間がかかっても; the later check has not yet happened.

exercises.context: Form practice: express even-if with the noun/na-adjective 不公平 and も; use でも.
exercises.line: ＿＿、{相手|あいて}を{傷|きず}つける{言葉|ことば}は{使|つか}いたくありません。
options: {不公平|ふこうへい}でも
{不公平|ふこうへい}だても
{不公平|ふこうへい}なても
exercises.explain: The nominal/na-adjective concessive form is でも, not だても or なても.

exercises.context: Form practice: complete the named noun pattern 条件なのに; do not choose between different concession constructions.
exercises.line: {同|おな}じ{条件|じょうけん}＿＿、{二人|ふたり}の{評価|ひょうか}が{違|ちが}います。
options: なのに
ののに
だのに
exercises.explain: In the standard pattern taught here, present nominal 条件 takes なのに.

exercises.context: Reply politely to Kenta: ask what he was testing, without assuming an excuse or a changed policy.
exercises.line: {今|いま}だけ、{字幕|じまく}を{消|け}していたんだ。
options: {何|なに}を{確認|かくにん}するために{消|け}したのか、{教|おし}えてください。
{説明|せつめい}を{聞|き}きません。{言|い}い{訳|わけ}だけですね。
{店|みせ}は{来年|らいねん}の{春|はる}に{開|ひら}きますね。
exercises.explain: The first asks for the actual test purpose. The others reject explanation or change the subject.

exercises.meaning: Even if preparation takes time, we will make the subtitles selectable.
tiles: {準備|じゅんび}に{時間|じかん}がかかっても、
exercises.explain: The preparation condition does not change the promised viewer choice; this is a forward action.

exercises.prompt: Which earlier wording does Misaki apologise for?
options: Saying “You said we could choose, and yet…” with blame
Asking where the café was
Explaining that the bus fare must be checked
exercises.explain: The opening explicitly quotes 言ったくせに and says 責めてしまった and ごめん.

exercises.prompt: Who acknowledges leaving out the explanation?
options: Kenta
The bus driver
A person not named in the scene
exercises.explain: Kenta says 説明を省略したのは俺だ.

exercises.prompt: What does Bao say the screen alone cannot reveal?
options: The other person’s real feelings or intention
Whether any subtitles were shown on that screen
Whether the café has two screens
exercises.explain: Bao contrasts the visible fact with inaccessible 本音/意図; no private intention is certified.

exercises.prompt: What is verified before starting the film?
options: Viewers can choose whether to display subtitles, and responsibilities are checked
The train suspension has been confirmed
The policy has permanently removed all subtitles
exercises.explain: Misaki checks viewer choice, and Kenta confirms the division and decision.

exercises.context: Recognition/form practice: in the quoted accusing expression 担当者のくせに, supply the noun attachment. This is not a recommended manager greeting.
exercises.line: 「{担当者|たんとうしゃ}＿＿くせに」という{言|い}い{方|かた}は{非難|ひなん}が{強|つよ}いです。
options: の
な
で
exercises.explain: A noun takes のくせに; a na-adjective takes なくせに.

exercises.context: Form practice: complete the stated な-adjective concession 不器用ながらも with its stem.
exercises.line: ＿＿ながらも、{気持|きも}ちを{丁寧|ていねい}に{伝|つた}えました。
options: {不器用|ぶきよう}
{不器用|ぶきよう}な
{不器用|ぶきよう}だ
exercises.explain: 不器用 is the stem before ながらも, without な or だ.

exercises.context: Reply to your friend in casual Japanese: accept making up and acknowledge your blaming wording.
options: うん。{責|せ}める{言|い}い{方|かた}をして、ごめんね。
いや。{説明|せつめい}は{聞|き}かない。
{電車|でんしゃ}の{終点|しゅうてん}は{知|し}らない。
exercises.explain: The first accepts reconciliation and apologises for blame; the others reject or change the topic.

exercises.meaning: Although the café is small, we can compare two screens.
tiles: {店|みせ}は{小|ちい}さいながらも、
exercises.explain: Limited size and comparison capacity coexist; this is not a two-action while sentence.

exercises.prompt: What happens before the film starts at three?
options: They apologise, make up and verify viewer subtitle choice
They announce a permanent ban on subtitles
They cancel the café gathering until next year
exercises.explain: The message states apologising, reconciliation, the choice check, then 三時に映画を始めた.
exercises.context: Find the completed sequence rather than an earlier complaint.

exercises.prompt: What conclusion does the writer explicitly avoid?
options: Claiming to know private feelings from the screen alone
Reporting that subtitles were missing on the first screen
Reporting Kenta’s stated test explanation
exercises.explain: The closing 本音は、画面だけでは分からない limits the inference; the other two are stated facts/reports.
exercises.context: Separate observation, someone’s explanation and private intention.

exercises.prompt: Which policy is kept even if preparation takes time?
options: Viewer choice about subtitles
No viewer may ever see subtitles
No explanation may be requested
exercises.explain: 時間がかかっても introduces the unchanged viewer-choice policy.
exercises.context: Track what the concession leaves unchanged.

watch.prompt: Optionally save a contrasting line from your own clip. Record what is stated, what is a speaker’s accusation, and how the listener responds. Do not turn tone or a saved line into a certified personality or proficiency score.
